newsitem.title: MEXICO: PRI running strong in Queretero state - poll.
newsitem.headline: PRI running strong in Queretero state - poll.

text.p: Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) will win at least 51 percent of the vote for governor in the state of Queretero in July 6 elections, according to a poll released on Wednesday.

"We're finding that 51 percent will vote for the PRI and about 36 percent for the PAN (National Action Party), that's for governor on a statewide level," Vicente Licona, director of the Indemerc Louis Harris polling firm, told a news conference.
Trailing them both is the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) with seven percent, Licona said.
The small state north of Mexico City is one of six that will choose a new governor on July 6, when Mexicans also will elect a new Congress, one-fourth of the Senate and a mayor for Mexico City.
"We view the tendency for governor completely irreversible," Licona said from the city of Queretero, capital of the state by the same name.
Licona said his firm interviewed 2,200 people in 86 places in all 18 cities in the state from May 31 to June 5, and that the poll had a margin of error of plus or minus three percent.
